title: Report Incidents in practice
intro: Fast reporting limits the damage. Decide what you would do in each moment from this module's lessons.

decisions.title: Your mailbox is 98% full
decisions.prompt: Look at the sender's address. What do you do with this e-mail?

artifact.subject: Your mailbox is 98% full
body: If you do not add space, new emails will be deleted in 24 hours.

decisions.explain: Your report lets specialists remove the same email from everyone else's inbox.

decisions.title: İşPoçt: Sign-in from a new device
decisions.prompt: If this sign-in was not you, what do you do?

artifact.title: İşPoçt: Sign-in from a new device
body: Someone signed in to your account from Ganja on an unknown device at 03:12.

decisions.explain: An unknown sign-in means someone has your password. Reporting fast saves the account.

decisions.title: Urgent: your account was hacked
decisions.prompt: Attackers sometimes write a second time. What do you do with this e-mail?

artifact.subject: Urgent: your account was hacked
body: After yesterday's incident, confirm your account again within one hour.

decisions.explain: The address is not your organisation's domain. Attackers often come back to the same person.

decisions.title: Security training on Friday
decisions.prompt: Should this be reported? Threat or normal?

artifact.subject: Security training on Friday
body: A short training takes place on Friday at 11:00 in the main hall. No registration needed.

decisions.explain: Correct address, no link, no request. This is a normal notice.

decisions.title: Staff list you just sent
decisions.prompt: You sent this a minute ago. Read the recipient. Is this an incident to report?

artifact.subject: Staff list
body: The list you asked for is attached.

decisions.explain: The list went to a personal address outside the organisation. That is a data leak, report it now.
